key_insight: Distributed neural controllers can boost plug-and-play network performance while preserving nominal stability through a guaranteed network gain bound at every training iterate.
engineering_relevance: This enables gradient-based tuning of neural control layers for changing networked systems without stability constraints or projection steps.
method: Use Internal Model Control–based Performance Boosting to reduce stability to a finite ℓ₂-gain requirement.
Map unconstrained trainable variables to gain-bounded neural operators that communicate only with neighboring subsystems.
Choose local compositional bounds for targeted updates after topology changes, or a network-norm bound for potentially less conservative design.
evidence_signal: A plug-and-play DC-microgrid case study reports improved voltage transients under topology changes and load variations while preserving nominal closed-loop stability.
watch_item: Local bounds may be conservative, while the network-norm alternative requires network-wide information; the stated stability guarantee is nominal.
paper_title: Distributed Performance Boosting through Neural Control for Plug-and-Play Networks
